newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 to 0.20 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 to 0.20 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 to 0.20 cent a lb lower on Tuesday based on market orders at 1018 EDT, traders said.
Traders said the latest spec/hedge report released this morning, which showed speculators were not as net short as expected, could dampen sentiment.

NYCE's weekly spec/hedge data showed the speculators to be holding a 14.8 percent net short position as of July 11, compared with a 20.6 percent net long position as of the previous week. Traders had expected the report to show speculators some 20 percent net short.
"The specs were not quite as short as we were thinking," said Frank Schneider and Co Inc analyst Sharon Johnson. "It may be a little negative to the market."
The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Monday said 60 percent of the cotton crop is in good to excellent condition, unchanged from the previous week.

Monday, the December contract ended 0.12 cent higher at 73.47 cents per lb, having ranged from 73.70 to 73.20 cents, a new life-of-contract low. The rest of the board finished 0.15 higher to 0.10 cent lower.
An estimated 7,000 lots changed hands on the day.
Support in December remained at 72.00 cents followed by 70.35 cents, the now-expired July contract low.
Some analysts said the market is oversold and should begin to retrace losses over the next several sessions. Resistance in December was pegged at 74.10 cents and then at 74.50 cents.
